findings.rationale: Document checking applies signed approval records without loading trust keys, verifying signatures, or checking their spec/rendering/claim-set bindings. A forged or stale approval plus a correspondingly rendered artifact can therefore be reported document_conformant, despite generation explicitly failing closed on unverifiable approvals.

The old model receives new bounds only for keys explicitly declared in both versions. Adding or removing a verify-bound leaves the old side at its original/default scope while the new side uses the new scope, even though the result claims comparison:"new". Semantic differences and CI gates can consequently be false negatives or false positives.

find_comparator iterates byte offsets and slices s[i..] at every offset. Any multibyte UTF-8 character before a comparator causes slicing at a non-character boundary and panics the CLI instead of returning an input diagnostic.

The block scanner and brace-depth routines recognize strings but not line comments. Braces or declaration-like text inside // comments can close a block early, fabricate a block, or produce an unterminated-block error for otherwise valid project source.

The project parser permits multiple ai_component declarations, but replay summarizes them into one mutable record. Each component header overwrites only the name without resetting fields, so --component rejects every component except the last and the last component can inherit contract fields from earlier components.

A dataset source embedded in a project is converted directly with PathBuf::from rather than resolved relative to the project file. The same project therefore reads a different file or fails depending on the caller's working directory.

Migration plans and semantic checks are computed from previously read contents, but the write phase verifies only that each target is currently a regular file. It never checks that the inode or contents are unchanged, so a concurrent edit between validation and rename is silently overwritten.

run_explain discards run_scenarios' status and always builds a successful explained envelope. Requirement-trace validation failures and solver/internal errors are thus converted into exit-0 output with missing witnesses instead of being propagated; HTML generation inherits this false-success path.
